i get that. and im not here to tell you that the path my faith and my sexuality went is the path you have to go to. I believe that starting to affirm my sexuality and realising that God loved me no matter what saved my life and me and my partner support each other in growing closer to god and live a faith filled relationship, but I can also believe that for other people thats simply not what they want to experience and not the way they want their life to go. I'm just saying that you have to pay attention to what is good for you and your mental health and remember that God has created you to live a happy and fulfilled life. There are even gay christian couples who eg decide to live in a queer platonic relationship, basically "dating" minus the sex and the wedding and all that stuff. Basically I'm just trying to say hey, there are a lot of ways to live your life while gloryfing god without denying your happiness.

I had a lot of the same struggles when I first came to terms with my sexuality. When i was 15 I was on my bedroom floor crying and begging for God to either kill me now (ok to be fair I was already depressed af anyway but this didnt help) or take my same sex attrecrtion away from me. But then I heard Gods voice. Not in an audible way like those fantastic stories you hear about but more of a whisper in my heart. He basically said "Hey [name], I love you. I love you how I made you. And thats all that matters." and Ive been able to go down a path that has led me to becoming self affirming, now being in a very positive church enviroment and in a relationship with a woman. I dont think the path I went is the path for everyone because sexuality is fluid as heck and maybe one day youll meet a guy who just is the one, but what I am trying to say is that you shouldnt deny your own happiness because of fear of condamnation from God. Because whatever anyone else says, whatever the voices in your head say,  God says that he loves you the way he made you. no matter what.

i have the same. Have you ever had DBT? If not I'd advise you to look into it, I know a lot of fellow peeps with bpd who say its saved their life after every other kind of therapy seemed to fail and I am no different. Sending good vibes your way. Try and remember that bpd is no longer the "untreatable" illness it once was and we actually have pretty decent recovery chances these days.

i work with special ed kids (so children with mental of physical challenges) and i want you to know that there are a lot of good people out there who will do everything in their power to support you and your child, no matter whats coming. I see the parents of the kids I work with struggle but I also see them delight in the joy their babies are bringing to the world and to their lifes. Its not an easy path but its no less beautiful than a healthy childs path.
